---
title: "Geog4/6300: Course learning standards"
format: html
---

## Data Literacy & Measurement
1. Classify variables by measurement type (nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio) and justify those classifications with reference to the characteristics of the data. (Lab 1)
2. Distinguish between vector and raster formats with spatial data. (Labs 2, 3)
3. Load tabular and spatial data into a code-based environment from multiple sources, including local files, remote APIs, and spatial file formats. (Labs 0, 1, 2, 3)
4. Identify and apply appropriate data filtering and cleaning strategies to prepare datasets for analysis, including handling missing or invalid responses. (Labs 0, 1, 3, 4)
5. Read and interpret existing code written by others, explaining in plain language what each step does to the data. (Lab 1)
6. Identify and use appropriate external documentation — including package references, help files, and peer resources — to learn and apply unfamiliar functions or methods. (Labs 0, 4)

## Data Wrangling & Transformation
7. Filter, aggregate, and transform datasets using grouping and summary operations to answer specific analytical questions. (Labs 0, 1, 2, 3)
8. Join multiple datasets using appropriate join strategies and explain how different join types affect the resulting output. (Labs 0, 2, 3)
9. Reshape data between wide and long formats to meet the requirements of different analytical or visualization tasks. (Labs 1, 3)
10. Derive new variables from existing ones through calculated transformations, including unit conversions, differences across time periods, and categorical dummy variables. (Labs 2, 3)

## Descriptive statistics and exploratory analysis
11. Create effective data visualizations across multiple chart types (line, scatter, histogram, Q-Q plot), applying appropriate aesthetic choices such as color, grouping, and labeling. (Labs 1, 3, 4, 5)
12. Produce and interpret confidence interval plots that enable visual comparison of means and uncertainty across groups or time periods. (Lab 3)
13. Visualize spatial data using appropriate mapping tools, selecting suitable classification schemes and cartographic elements to support clear communication. (Labs 2, 3, 4, 6)
14. Arrange and present tabular results in a readable format appropriate for a technical document or report. (Labs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
15. Use measures of central tendancy and dispersion to describe the variables in tabular datasets (Labs 1, 3)

## Spatial Analysis
16. Load, manipulate, and perform mathematical operations on raster data, including multi-layer operations and unit conversions. (Lab 2)
17. Convert between spatial data types (e.g., non-spatial to spatial, vector/raster) to enable different forms of spatial analysis. (Labs 2, 4)
18. Apply zonal statistics to extract summary values from raster data for polygon and point vector datasets, and integrate those results with attribute data. (Labs 2, 3)
19. Calculate and interpret descriptive spatial statistics such as mean center, and connect the geographic distribution of observations to patterns in the data. (Lab 2)

## Inferential Statistics
20. Explaining how evidence from a sample supports conclusions about a population while acknowledging sampling variability and uncertainty. (Labs 3, 4, 5)
21. Assess the normality of a variable using multiple diagnostic approaches and use those results to select between parametric and non-parametric statistical tests. (Labs 4, 5)
22. Construct and interpret confidence intervals, explaining how factors such as sample size and spatial scale affect the precision of an estimate. (Lab 3)
23. Apply two-sample tests of difference and accurately interpret results in terms of hypothesis testing, statistical significance, and the direction and magnitude of any differences. (Lab 4)
24. Construct contingency tables and apply chi-square tests to assess association between categorical variables, interpreting results in terms of significance and practical meaning. (Lab 4)
25. Conduct correlation analysis across multiple variable pairs and evaluate results with respect to direction, magnitude, and significance, including changes in correlation structure across time periods or subgroups. (Lab 5)
26. Build and interpret univariate and multivariate OLS regression models, explaining the role of each coefficient and evaluating overall model fit. (Lab 6)
27. Diagnose regression model assumptions by assessing residuals for normality, spatial autocorrelation, heteroskedasticity, and multicollinearity, and explain the implications of any violations for model interpretation. (Lab 6)

## Communication & Reproducibility
28. Communicate statistical findings clearly in writing for a general audience, situating results in their geographic and social context, and use a reproducible document format to integrate code, output, and narrative in a single deliverable. (Labs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)

## Competency with R and programming
29. Recognize and be able to manipulate multiple data object types (vectors, data frames, or lists). (Labs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
30. Develop abilities to appropriately load a variety of spatial and non-spatial data formats. (Labs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
31. Effectively navigate the R and RStudio interface. (Labs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
32. Use Git and Github to create and share project materials in a repository format. (Labs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
